senses.definition: Chromium, when used to plate other metals.
(graphical user interface) The basic structural elements used in a graphical user interface, such as window frames and scroll bars, as opposed to the content.

quotes.text: So, just as a car might have shiny chrome trimming, a bumper, and a grill that cover the vehicle, so the chrome of an OS window surrounds and complements the window itself. Examples of chrome include the title bar, the Minimize/Maximize/Restore buttons, menu bars, and toolbars.
quotes.reference: 2009, Richard Wagner, Adobe AIR For Dummies, John Wiley & Sons, →ISBN:

quotes.text: Similarly [to the chrome exterior of an automobile], in most modern GUIs, the chrome lives around the edges of the screen, surrounding the middle area, which is dedicated to the user's data.
quotes.reference: 2012 January 29, Jakob Nielsen, “Browser and GUI Chrome”, in Nielsen Norman Group homepage, Nielsen Norman Group, archived from the original on 07 Mar 2013:

quotes.text: I had the idea of making our browser chrome match the actual hardware you were on. If your Mac’s bezel was Bondi blue, we’d make our UI Bondi blue.
quotes.reference: 2020 January 4, Jimmy Grewal, quoting Maf Vosburgh, “Internet Explorer 5 for Mac: twentieth anniversary”, in Jimmy's Blog, archived from the original on 09 Jan 2020:

quotes.text: Disrespect my nigga Boss and I'm flashin' the chrome
quotes.reference: 2012, “Ali Bomaye”, in Jesus Piece, performed by The Game:

quotes.text: I ain't trippin' long 'cause I can reach the chrome / Heat your home like Southern California Gas, police pass
quotes.reference: 2013, “Hive”, in Doris, performed by Earl Sweatshirt:
